name: Hot water, hot food and pepper soup after birth
what_people_do: For weeks after birth the mother drinks hot water, eats hot (temperature) and very peppery food and bathes in hot water.
why_they_say_it_works: Birth is believed to leave the body "cold" and "open"; heat restores it and helps the milk.

documented_by.source: Udigwe GO, Emelumadu OF, Udigwe IB 2013, West Afr J Med, PMID 24488282
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Nnewi, 330 Igbo mothers: 81.8% regularly drank hot water, 85.5% bathed in hot water, 81.8% took hot food and 75.8% took very peppery food.

evidence.finding: My search found no study of the regimen as a whole.

source.name: agent4-traditional-practices.md, 12 Nov 2026 (research file in this project)

harm_note: The Nnewi authors judged some of the practices in their list to be dangerous; the abstract does not say which, and I did not read the full text.
gaps: "Omugwo" (the Igbo postpartum care custom) not searched by name.
